title: The Autopsy of the Fens
premise: True-crime podcaster Marguerite Vane has spent seven years documenting the disappearance of Elowen Marsh, a fenland girl who vanished in 1998, treating the case as her life's safest obsession. When a waterlogged diary surfaces in the drained fens—its entries continuing three years past the date Elowen supposedly died—Marguerite realizes the town's tidy narrative was a burial, and that someone alive helped write it. As she follows the diary's coded references through the marsh's drowned villages, she uncovers a survival pact among four teenagers who sacrificed a fifth to escape their circumstances, and discovers her own family's name inked in its margins. The final entry is dated next week. In the climax at the flooded chapel, Marguerite confronts the last surviving pact member—her own mother, who has been feeding her clues to force a confession before dying—and must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy them both or letting the fens keep their dead.
about_author: Jonah Reyes is the pen name of a former court stenographer from East Anglia who spent fifteen years transcribing testimony in cases no one remembers. The Autopsy of the Fens is their first novel, drawn from the silences they learned to hear between spoken words.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Marguerite Vane records the final episode of her stalled podcast on the 1998 disappearance of Elowen Marsh, cataloguing her archive of the case like a museum curator. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: controlled detachment masking seven years of grief-adjacent obsession; she closes the file, believing the story is over.

chapters.title: What the Drainage Uncovered
chapters.summary: A fenland drainage crew unearths a tin box containing Elowen Marsh's diary, delivered to Marguerite by a guilt-ridden foreman. The last legible entry is dated 2001—three years after Elowen vanished. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: vertigo; the closed case yawns open beneath her.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot on Purpose
chapters.summary: Marguerite returns to the fen town of Saltmere, interviewing residents whose rehearsed answers reveal a community that agreed to remember nothing. An old constable warns her off. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: creeping unease as hospitality curdles into collective denial.

chapters.title: Entries in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Forensic examination shows the post-disappearance diary entries are written in two hands: Elowen's deteriorating script and a second, steadier one. Marguerite realizes someone kept writing for—or as—the missing girl. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: fascination tipping toward dread.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Summer
chapters.summary: Digging into 1998 school records, Marguerite identifies Elowen's tight circle: Ruth Calloway, Peter Ives, Dana Okafor, and her own mother, Sylvie Vane. All four still live within twenty miles of the fens. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: betrayal's first cold touch—her mother's name in the margins of everything.

chapters.title: Ruth, Who Prays for Closure
chapters.summary: Ruth Calloway, now a church volunteer, gives a tearful interview that contradicts her own 1998 statement. That night someone ransacks Marguerite's rental car but takes only the diary's photographs. POV: alternating Marguerite and Ruth. Emotional beat: fear arriving in earnest; the past defends itself.

chapters.title: Peter Ives Drowns
chapters.summary: Before Marguerite can interview him, Peter Ives is found dead in a drainage channel—an apparent accident that mirrors details only the diary contains. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: horror hardening into resolve; the diary isn't history, it's a countdown.

chapters.title: The Pact in the Chapel
chapters.summary: Decoding diary references to a 'chapel under water,' Marguerite finds records of a submerged chapel where five teens met in summer 1998—not four. A fifth name, scrubbed from every record: Ada Fenwick. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: revelation's thrill shadowed by the question of what happened to the fifth girl.

chapters.title: Dana's Confession, Half-Spoken
chapters.summary: Dana Okafor, terminally ill, tells Marguerite about the pact: five runaways pooling money to flee Saltmere, an argument on the night of departure, and waking to find one of them gone. She refuses to say who did what. POV: Dana then Marguerite. Emotional beat: pity entangled with suspicion; everyone survived something terrible.

chapters.title: My Mother's Steady Hand
chapters.summary: Handwriting comparison confirms the second hand in the diary belongs to Sylvie Vane. Confronted, Sylvie admits she wrote the later entries—but claims she was transcribing letters Elowen sent her until 2001. Letters that stopped. POV: alternating Marguerite and Sylvie. Emotional beat: the ground of family trust cracking open.

chapters.title: Ada Fenwick, Alive on Paper
chapters.summary: Marguerite traces Ada Fenwick to a new identity in Norwich—a woman who changed her name the same week the diary entries ended. When Marguerite knocks, the house is empty except for a packed bag and a photograph of the five teens. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: hope curdling; Ada isn't hiding from the past, she's running from the present.

chapters.title: The Episode That Shouldn't Air
chapters.summary: Marguerite drafts an episode naming the pact members; within hours, her editor pulls it under legal pressure traced to Saltmere's most prominent family—the Ives estate, which Peter's death just enriched. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: fury and clarity; the cover-up has money, and money has patience.

chapters.title: Sylvie's Diagnosis
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers her mother has been hiding a terminal diagnosis and a folder of research on Elowen's case—decades deeper than any podcaster's. Sylvie has been investigating alone since 2001. POV: Sylvie. Emotional beat: grief reframed; her mother wasn't concealing guilt but conducting a vigil.

chapters.title: The Night of the Departure
chapters.summary: Piecing together testimony, Marguerite reconstructs the pact's final night: the plan to leave, the theft of the pooled money, and Elowen following the thief into the fens. One of the five never intended to leave at all. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the shape of the crime emerging—betrayal before violence.

chapters.title: Letters from a Living Girl
chapters.summary: Sylvie produces the letters Elowen allegedly sent until 2001. Marguerite recognizes phrases lifted verbatim from the diary—including a detail about the chapel that only the killer would know. Either Elowen lived, or her killer kept writing. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: whiplash between hope and horror; the same evidence proves both.

chapters.title: Ruth Breaks
chapters.summary: Cornered with the letters' inconsistencies, Ruth confesses her role: she helped bury the truth of that night but swears Elowen walked away alive, heading for the chapel. Her terror isn't of exposure—it's of whoever Elowen went to meet. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: confession as relief and dread braided together.

chapters.title: The Last Entry Is Next Week
chapters.summary: Marguerite decodes the diary's final undated fragment: coordinates in the fens and a date seven days out—the anniversary ritual the pact observed yearly, which this year only one member could attend. She realizes the diary was left to be found now, deliberately. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut around her even as she springs it.

chapters.title: Who Kept Writing
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing paper stock and ink, Marguerite concludes the post-1998 entries were written by someone keeping Elowen's voice alive—either a captor maintaining a fiction or Elowen herself, hidden all these years inside Saltmere. Both suspects converge on one address. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: obsessive clarity; she knows where, not yet who.

chapters.title: Into the Drained Fens
chapters.summary: On the anniversary eve, Marguerite walks the drained channels to the exposed chapel ruins, followed at a distance by Sylvie. There she finds Ada Fenwick waiting—alive, aged, and holding the original pages the diary excerpts were copied from. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: threshold dread; the story's buried heart finally above water.

chapters.title: The Autopsy
chapters.summary: In the chapel, Ada reveals the truth: Elowen died accidentally fleeing the money-thief, and Ada—spared because she ran—has spent decades as the keeper of the pact's secret, writing in Elowen's hand to hold the others to silence. The thief was Sylvie, who took the money to fund her own escape and has been paying ever since. POV: Ada then Marguerite. Emotional beat: devastating symmetry—every survivor paid a different price for the same night.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Sylvie arrives and confesses publicly, recording enabled, choosing exposure over the slow death her illness promised. Marguerite must decide whether to air the episode that destroys her mother and frees Ada, or bury the tape as the town always has. She airs it. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: climax of choice—the price of survival finally named and paid.

chapters.title: The Final Entry
chapters.summary: Months later, Marguerite publishes the podcast's true final episode and writes the closing line in the recovered diary herself, returning it to the fens. Ada, freed by the truth, visits Elowen's marked grave as the waters rise again. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: mournful resolution—memory restored, identity reclaimed, and the cost of survival acknowledged without absolution.
